cells.tense: Right now you're moving through what isn't clear yet, and you're not forcing it to be.
cells.ask: Offer the next step to what you're tending, and let the direction come from being genuinely in it — see what steady warmth gives back.
cells.core:
You make your way through uncertainty by feel, and that's working. It looks like a kitchen at dusk with no plan for the evening — you taste, you adjust, you find out what you're making by making it. You stay with the not-knowing instead of rushing past it, and what you touch comes back warm because you were actually there for it.

What you're free to feed next is staying power — not more vision, but the warmth that keeps a direction alive after the first spark has gone. The path has been showing itself, one step at a time. Something in you can decide to keep walking it, and that decision is yours to make while the light is still here.

cells.tense: You're leaning into a future you haven't felt yet, and you're straining to see past the part that isn't written.
cells.ask: Let one thing you're steering grow at its own pace today — hold it without gripping — and notice the steadiness that comes back.
cells.core:
Tending a garden you can't hurry is what this is when it's working — you water, you wait, and the growth is real because you didn't yank it. You trust the next step to show up when you get there, and the work stays alive under your hands.

Here, though, you're reaching for four steps ahead of where anyone can actually stand. You see what isn't there yet so clearly that you're already living in it, and the strain is pulling you out of the part you can feel. Tea should steep. The next thing in front of you wants your hands, not your worry about how it will all look from the far end.

cells.tense: You've been treating this as a path you can't walk, though nothing here is actually closing.
cells.ask: Ask one real question about where you're going and stay curious about the answer — let the wanting-to-know pull the step through.
cells.core:
Moving through fog with just the next few feet in view is how this goes when it's clean — you go slower, you feel the ground, and you trust that trust itself is the way. You let the unknown stay unknown a beat longer than most people can stand, and the ground meets you anyway.

Lately the weight has been on pushing forward instead of noticing, and so the whole thing feels closed off. What brings it back isn't a bigger effort in the dark. It's a question you actually want answered, held with beginner's patience, and letting what you notice lead you to the next move.

cells.tense: You're already moving through uncertainty right now, but the claim on how you got here isn't yours.
cells.ask: Put a name on one insight you've been crediting to luck or circumstance, and finish it with your own hand.
cells.core:
When something is being made here it's like cooking with no written recipe and tasting as you go — you adjust, you invent, you finish by feel. You build like that daily, and the results hold because the feeling was doing real work under your hands the whole time.

But you keep attributing the moves to chance. The flow of imagination that should feel like yours reads as something that happened to you. Claiming it means going back to the simplest form of this — rigorous practice, plain method, your own groundwork — and letting that be where your knowing comes from, out loud, as the one who did it.
cells.sheetLine: Your way through this is running. Your claim on it isn't.
